questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I've always liked the cultural environment i Berlin, and so I wanted to live there.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I thougth the process was a bit diffucult because you receive many different emails and with much information. Getting the info is not necessarily hard but you have to stay on top of your email-inbox.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were some introductury meetings and a guided tour of the university, which was helpful. There were also a lot off emails - so make sure that youve read all your mail on zedat.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: For me it was pretty easy as I had a contact who owned an apartment in Berlin. Generally it can be difficult to find housing on websites, so I would suggest reaching out to the people around you or people who went on exchange in Berlin.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Even though its hard to find housing, try to find housing off campus, as you'll get to know the city far better. Also you have to make your anmeldung in time.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are some dorms, but there were far away from the city and i've mostly heard negative things about them, so I wouldn't recommend it.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You just go to courses the first weeks and see which ones you find interesring. After that you either register on CampusManagement or just talk to the professor.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: To be honest I don't really remember, but the process is fairly easy, so don't be worried.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the courses that I wanted, so it was pretty succesful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think you should take the courses which sounds the most interesting. You won't have your grades transferres, so just try to learn new things.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I thought the level of the courses was pretty high - maybe a bit higher than KU. The readings were a lot shorter but also a more diffucult I think. But you also have to do a lot of homework, though it's not that time consuming.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was definetly much more fluid and interactive than the style of teaching at KU. The students played a much larger role, so it paid to have the readings.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Late Fascism
Ghosts and hauting theories and the mena region
Global south feminisms
Democracy and political meritocracy

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Late Fascism with Jan Slaby. The readings on the course were just very interesting and the topic was really relevant in our time. Also the other students were very talented.

questions.answer: A bike is really nice to have

questions.answer: Eating out and drinking is cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I didn't really participate in that stuff, but if you really want to go, there endless social activities through erasmus and other student orgnisations.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Just walk around in the city and experiencing the different areas. Try some good döner maybe and drink cheap and good beers at a späti.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go clubbing. The nightlife in Berlin is great. Or just go to some of the markets around town. Or go for a swin in the lakes.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. I've been to Berlin many times, so I knew what to expect. Also german culture and danish culture isn't radically different.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I'm not the best at socializing with other students, but just talk to them. People are pretty nice and more open than danish people i would say.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really anything. The culture is quite similar to the danish culture.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The nightlife and just the casual and laid back culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Take the courses which sound fun
2. Try to find an apartment and a cool area  - use your network
3. Enjoy the city and don't spend all your time studying. Find the right balance.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The Mensa has some good french fries. There language courses at freie are really expensive - you can find other alternatives cheaper.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I really liked trying to live abroad. Also I just like german culture and Berlin as a city, so it was a priviledge staying there for half a year.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding time to do everything you want to do. It can be hard to prioritize. Also you should consider how many friends you wan't to visit you. It's of course great having your friends in the city, but if you have visitors in back to back weekends it can be exhausting - spread it throughout your stay.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
